rawFindings.title: Incorrect handling of object with $class and $ null properties in v1 encoder
rawFindings.explanation: The original code had a condition to treat objects with a string $class and null $ property as null during encoding. This was removed in the new code, potentially changing semantics and causing encoding differences for such objects.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the check for is.string(obj.$class) && is.nullOrUndefined(obj.$) in the condition to preserve original behavior for null-valued typed objects.

rawFindings.title: Removed tests for encoding null property objects with $class in object.test.js
rawFindings.explanation: Tests verifying encoding behavior of objects with properties having $class and null $ values were removed. This reduces coverage on a subtle encoding scenario relevant for backward compatibility.
rawFindings.suggestion: Retain or replace the removed tests to ensure coverage of encoding objects with nested typed null properties.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect removal of null property handling in writeObject
rawFindings.explanation: The original code in lib/v1/encoder.js checked for objects where obj.$class is a string and obj.$ is null or undefined, and treated them as null (return null). This special handling was removed in the patch, which can cause wrong encoding behavior when encoding objects like { $class: 'xxx', $: null }, possibly resulting in invalid encoding or errors.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the original condition in writeObject: if (is.nullOrUndefined(obj) || (is.string(obj.$class) && is.nullOrUndefined(obj.$))) { return null; }

rawFindings.title: Incorrect null handling check in writeObject
rawFindings.explanation: The original code's condition to check if the object is null or has '$class' string but null/undefined '$' property was removed, now only is.nullOrUndefined(obj) is checked. This changes behavior and can cause improper encoding of objects with $class and $ properties that have null values.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the original condition for null handling, including checking if obj is null or undefined, or if obj.$class is a string and obj.$ is null/undefined, to maintain previous serialization behavior.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect handling of objects with $class and $ properties in proto.writeObject
rawFindings.explanation: The original code excludes objects where is.string(obj.$class) && is.nullOrUndefined(obj.$), treating them as null. The new code only excludes nullOrUndefined(obj), so objects like {$class: 'xxx', $: null} will not be treated as null but encoded as objects. This changes semantics and breaks compatibility with tests that expect such objects to be encoded as null.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the original condition to check for is.string(obj.$class) && is.nullOrUndefined(obj.$) alongside is.nullOrUndefined(obj) to preserve previous behavior:
